setup: Sit on the floor with your torso upright.
Position your lead leg in front of you with the hip externally rotated and the knee bent at 90 degrees, resting flat on the ground.
Position your trail leg to the side with the hip internally rotated and the knee bent at 90 degrees, foot pointing behind you.
steps: Sit tall through the crown of your head and square your torso over the front shin.
Gently hinge forward from the hips with a flat back toward the front shin until a stretch is felt in the lead hip and glute.
Alternatively, press the rear hip toward the floor to target internal rotation in the back hip.
Hold the position for the desired duration, breathing slowly, then switch leg positions and repeat.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply, using slow exhales to relax deeper into the stretch without forcing range of motion.
cues: Hinge at the hips, not the lower back
Keep both knees bent at 90 degrees

common_faults.fault: Rounding the spine excessively to reach further toward the floor.
common_faults.correction: Keep your chest tall and pivot strictly from the hip crease.

common_faults.fault: Knees drifting into sharp flexion less than 90 degrees.
common_faults.correction: Check your shin angles to maintain true 90-degree angles at both knee joints.

common_faults.fault: Forcing the trail hip into internal rotation causing knee or lower back pain.
common_faults.correction: Elevate your pelvis on a yoga block or cushion to reduce torque on the hip and knee.

precautions: Do not force end-range hip internal rotation if sharp pain is felt in the groin or knee joint.

name: 90-90 Hip Stretch
summary: A seated hip mobility stretch performed with both legs bent at right angles to improve internal and external hip rotation.
